name: Pébay pairwise centered cross moment merge
definition: For disjoint nonempty paired blocks G=A,B, C_G=Σ_(i∈G)(x_i−m_(x,G))(y_i−m_(y,G)); n=n_A+n_B, δ_x=m_(x,B)−m_(x,A), δ_y=m_(y,B)−m_(y,A); C=C_A+C_B+δ_xδ_y n_A n_B/n
variables: C_G unnormalized centered cross moment; m_(x,G),m_(y,G) block coordinate means; n_G positive counts; C merged cross moment
assumptions: Disjoint observation identities with aligned finite real pairs, consistent block summaries, common coordinate units, exact counts and representable intermediates; identity in real arithmetic
limitations: Products and mean differences may overflow or underflow or suffer cancellation; merge order matters in floating point; covariance does not establish independence or causation
failure_conditions: Unpaired observations, overlapping identities, inconsistent states, or nonfinite intermediates
Attempt to normalize by n−1 for n<2
computation: Merge both coordinate means using the count-weighted Chan update, then add the between-block product correction to the two cross moments. Return the unnormalized state; divide by n for empirical covariance or n−1 for sample covariance when n≥2 and the inferential assumptions are justified. An empty block is handled as an identity without using its undefined means.

source.citation: Pébay (2008), Formulas for Robust, One-Pass Parallel Computation of Covariances and Arbitrary-Order Statistical Moments, SAND2008-6212, pp. 12–13, Proposition 3.1, eqs. (3.1)–(3.11). DOI 10.2172/1028931. https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc837537/m2/1/high_res_d/1028931.pdf

application: General numerical covariance summary; no empirical benefit claimed.
incompatible_methods: Treating a rounded cross moment as exact
mechanism_note: Expanding each centered product about the combined means eliminates both first-order terms because within-block deviations sum to zero. Setting y=x recovers Chan's second-moment merge. This is its bivariate extension rather than a new distinct algorithm.

name: Pébay arbitrary-order central moment merge
definition: For integer p≥3 and disjoint nonempty blocks G=A,B, n=n_A+n_B, m=m_A+(m_B−m_A)n_B/n, M_(j,G)=Σ_(i∈G)(x_i−m_G)^j for j≥2; M_p=Σ_(j=0)^p binom(p,j)[M_(j,A)(m_A−m)^(p−j)+M_(j,B)(m_B−m)^(p−j)], with M_(0,G)=n_G, M_(1,G)=0 and exponent-zero factors equal to 1
variables: p integer moment order; M_(j,G) unnormalized block central moment; m_G block mean; n_G positive count; m and M_p merged mean and moment
assumptions: Finite real observations, disjoint observation identities, consistent lower-order moment states, exact counts, and representable intermediate terms; identity in real arithmetic
limitations: Large powers and binomial coefficients may overflow or underflow; cancellation and merge order affect floating-point accuracy; high-order moments are sensitive to outliers and are not inherently robust
failure_conditions: Missing lower moments, invalid counts, overlapping blocks or nonfinite intermediates
Treating normalized moments as unnormalized states without conversion
computation: Compute combined mean and the two mean shifts; evaluate the binomial sum from the unchanged input states. Use exponent-zero factors of 1 even for zero shifts. Compute each needed order before replacing block states; empty blocks are identities handled separately. Divide by n only if an empirical normalized moment is desired.

source.citation: Pébay (2008), Formulas for Robust, One-Pass Parallel Computation of Covariances and Arbitrary-Order Statistical Moments, SAND2008-6212, p. 10, Proposition 2.1, particularly eq. (2.6). DOI 10.2172/1028931. https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc837537/m2/1/high_res_d/1028931.pdf

application: General numerical higher-moment summary; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Disjoint block counts, means and moments through the declared order.
incompatible_methods: Treating high-order moments as robust estimators
mechanism_note: Apply the binomial theorem to x_i−m=(x_i−m_G)+(m_G−m) and sum separately over the blocks. Re-indexing the exponent gives the stated form of (2.6); the first centered moment vanishes. At p=2 this reduces to Chan's merge, so arbitrary higher orders are a single variant, not separate entries per order.
